content: The initial treatment involves administering 200 mg of acyclovir orally every 4 hours while awake (5 times daily) for 10 days, or alternatively, 400 mg orally every 8 hours for 7 to 10 days. For intermittent treatment of recurrent episodes, 200 mg is given orally every 4 hours while awake (5 times daily) for 5 days, starting at the earliest sign or symptom of recurrence. Chronic suppression of recurrent episodes can be achieved with 400 mg orally every 12 hours for up to 12 months, or alternatively, 200 mg orally 3 to 5 times daily. Intravenous (IV) dosing of 10 to 15 mg/kg every 8 hours for 10 days has been reported, with durations of up to 14 to 21 days in some cases. In immunocompromised patients, IV dosing of 5 mg/kg every 8 hours for 7 days is recommended, with durations of up to 14 days reported. Off-label oral dosing involves 400 mg every 4 hours while awake (5 times daily) for 7 days. For acute treatment in immunocompetent patients weighing more than 40 kg, 800 mg orally every 6 hours for 5 days is recommended. In immunocompromised patients, IV dosing of 10 to 15 mg/kg every 8 hours for 7 to 10 days is used, with dose adjustments based on renal clearance and the dosage form. For neonates with a postmenstrual age (PMA) of ≥34 weeks, 20 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 21 days is recommended. For neonates with a PMA of <34 weeks, the same dose is given every 12 hours for 21 days. Caution is advised if renal dysfunction beyond the effects of prematurity occurs. For children aged 3 months to 12 years, 20 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 10 days is recommended, with durations of up to 14 to 21 days reported. For patients aged ≥12 years, 10 to 15 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 14 to 21 days is used. In immunocompromised children under 12 years, 10 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 7 days is recommended. For immunocompetent patients aged ≥12 years, 800 mg orally every 4 hours while awake (5 times daily) for 7 to 10 days is used. For immunocompromised patients aged ≥12 years, 30 mg/kg/day IV divided every 8 hours for 7 to 10 days is recommended. For children aged ≥2 years and weighing <40 kg, 20 mg/kg/dose orally every 6 hours for 5 days is used, not exceeding 800 mg per dose. For those weighing ≥40 kg, 800 mg orally every 6 hours for 5 days is recommended. Ideal body weight (IBW) should be used for obese patients. Drug interactions with acyclovir include increased nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity when combined with amphotericin B deoxycholate, bacitracin, cidofovir, neomycin, amikacin, capreomycin, carboplatin, cisplatin, colistin, iodinated contrast media, cyclosporine, gentamicin, polymyxin B, streptomycin, and vancomycin. These combinations should be avoided or monitored closely. Acyclovir may also decrease the effects of talimogene laherparepvec due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, and caution is advised when co-administering these agents. Acyclovir can increase the levels of drugs such as amoxicillin, emtricitabine, tenofovir, mycophenolate, and peramivir by reducing renal clearance. Co-administration with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum concentrations of these agents, necessitating caution and monitoring. Minor interactions with drugs such as aspirin, ibuprofen, diclofenac, and other acidic (anionic) drugs may increase acyclovir levels due to competition for renal tubular clearance, though the clinical significance of these interactions is often unknown.
